messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High request spike detected on /v2/embeddings (prod, embeddings-v2). 8.3x baseline traffic over last 5m, error rate 12% (429/5xx), tail latency 95th=1.8s. Top source region: apac-3. Pager: https://pager.example/INC-8912
sara (oncall): acked. I'm on it, pinging eng-sre and infra. Can someone grab traffic breakdown and top IP CIDRs? :eyes:
leo (eng-sre): looking now. initial glance — huge fanout of small requests, lots of concurrent sessions from a small set of client IP ranges. I see repeated patterns that look like automated scraping (very short inter-request TTL).
tom (eng-infra): agree. logs show many clients hitting embeddings batch endpoint with size=1 and no client-side backoff. I'm prepping a quick WAF block and a region rate policy.
maria (support): support is already seeing customer reports: several customers (acct_4721, acct_9982) see 429s when sending bulk embed jobs. CS is triaging — impact: some queued jobs failing, others delayed.
anya (product): please estimate customer impact % and whether we should post a status notice. If this hits larger customers we should notify.
leo (eng-sre): tentative plan: 1) apply geo-rate-limit for apac-3 to 50 r/s for embeddings-v2 2) add temporary WAF CIDR block for the most aggressive /24 3) disable batching of size=1 (force minimum batch window) to reduce backend churn. I'll coordinate with infra for commands.
tom (eng-infra): commands I'm going to run now:
```
# block offending CIDR
wafctl add-block 203.0.113.0/24 --reason "scraper spike apac-3" --ttl 30m
# apply regional rate policy
routectl set-policy embeddings-v2 --region apac-3 --rate-limit 50r/s --burst 100
# disable tiny-batches to force batching window
servicectl update embeddings-router --min-batch-size 4 --batch-window 25ms
```
I'll stage the WAF rule then flip routing after confirmation.
leo (eng-sre): I'm going to add a quick rate-slice as well to protect control plane: `quotactl slice --service embeddings-v2 --slice apac-3 --limit 2000/min`. This keeps overall per-tenant quotas intact but caps noisy region.
sara (oncall): if you apply the WAF please paste the rule ID here so we can revert after. Also update the incident channel when done.
tom (eng-infra): WAF rule applied -> rule id w-r-78341 :white_check_mark: Starting routectl now.
leo (eng-sre): route policy applied. temporarily set to 50 r/s for apac-3. I'm also toggling embedding-batching to min size 4. :wrench:
maria (support): customer impact check: reduced error reports after the block but two enterprise customers still see degraded throughput (acct_4721, acct_1145). CS has opened high-priority tickets and asked for ETA.
anya (product): ok we should prepare a short status update: "We are mitigating a high-volume automated traffic spike impacting embeddings in APAC. Temporary rate limits and WAF blocks are in place; some customers may see delayed embedding jobs. Investigating; will update." Approve?
sara (oncall): approve. post to status page and add note to support template.
ops-runner-bot: posted to status page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/INC-8912
leo (eng-sre): two follow-ups: 1) enable passive KV prefix caching for popular prefixes to avoid recompute 2) capture sample client user agents and sign-up patterns to feed abuse team. I'll dump UA list in a minute.
tom (eng-infra): enabled passive cache layer via `cachectl enable embeddings-prefix --ttl 20m` — should cut repeat work for identical inputs.
leo (eng-sre): UA sample: "curl/7.78.0" repeated but also custom bot signatures. saving to s3://incidents/8912/ua-sample.txt.
maria (support): CS confirms reduced 429s after mitigations but a backlog exists. ETA for backlog drain ~2 hours with current throughput. We're drafting notice to affected customers (apologize + ETA).
anya (product): we should consider rate-limiting by token-per-request for bulk jobs in long-term to avoid single clients spiking cost. Adding to backlog.
sara (oncall): handoff plan: I'll remain on-call for 30m to confirm stability, then hand to leo for next 4 hours. Please ensure runbook steps for reverting WAF and batch changes are documented in the incident ticket.
leo (eng-sre): noted. I'll own the postmortem. Short-term next steps: monitor tail latency and error rate, confirm backlog drain, gather list of offending IPs/UA for legal/abuse. Medium-term: consider adaptive client-side throttles and per-api token rate enforcement.
tom (eng-infra): logging note: capture packet counts for blocked CIDR for 30m so we can tune TTL.
ops-runner-bot: scheduled follow-up check-in in 30m.
sara (oncall): thanks team. leaving a final note here before handoff: immediate mitigations applied (WAF block id w-r-78341, regional rate applied, batching min adjusted, passive cache enabled). Monitoring shows error rate down from 12% -> 1.6% in last 5m. handing off to leo now. :white_check_mark:
sara (oncall): @maria please coordinate customer comms with the support template we approved.
maria (support): will do. drafting now and will link the notices in the ticket.
leo (eng-sre): taking over. will run deeper analysis and open postmortem skeleton. thanks.
notes: short-term WAF block + regional rate-limiting + batching tweak + passive cache; handoff performed
